messages.content: Explain why the Moon appears to change shape during a month.

response: The Moon appears to change shape over the course of a month because the Sun illuminates different portions of the Moon's face as the Moon orbits the Earth. The Moon does not produce its own light — what we see from Earth is the side of the Moon that is facing us reflecting sunlight. As the Moon moves around the Earth, different portions of it are entering or exiting the Earth's shadow or are facing toward or away from the Sun. Specifically, the cycle of Moon phases is caused by the relative positions of the Earth, Moon, and Sun. When the Moon is on the same side of the Earth as the Sun, the side facing us is mostly in darkness and we see a new moon. As the Moon moves to the side, more of its daylight side becomes visible to us — this is the waxing crescent, waxing gibbous, full moon, and waning gibbous, ending back at new moon. The apparent circularity of the Moon is actually an illusion; its shape is always a sphere, but only one face is visible to us from any given spot on Earth.
